title: Fibre degree bounds multiply under composition (Stacks 03J6)
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. If the integer $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ and the integer $m$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $g$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound], then $nm$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $g\circ f:X\to Z$: for every $z\in Z$ the fibre $X_z=X\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ of $g\circ f$ is finite over $\kappa(z)$ with $\dim_{\kappa(z)}\Gamma(X_z,\mathcal O_{X_z})\le nm$. In particular a composition of morphisms with universally bounded fibres has universally bounded fibres.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371, and its proof

proof.text: Fix z, let gz be the finite fibre projection of g and let fz be the pullback of f along the inclusion of that fibre. The base-change bound gives BoundsFiberDegrees fz n.

Prove fz finite: finite fibres imply LocallyQuasiFinite by Mathlib LocallyQuasiFinite.of_fiberToSpecResidueField. The target is Artinian since it is finite over a field. The source is a finite union of the finite underlying fibres, transported by fiberHomeo, hence finite and compact. It is quasi-compact over the affine target. Mathlib IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite now applies. This is the fully proved private helper finite_of_finite_fibers_over_field.

Paste the two pullback squares using IsPullback.paste_vert. Its isoPullback identifies fz followed by gz with the composite fibre projection, and transports finiteness and finrankΓ via finrankΓ_eq_of_iso.

Apply the finite-field tower degree estimate to fz, gz and their degree bound n. Then multiply the bound finrankΓ gz <= m by n and use transitivity, giving n*m. For the existential clause, choose n and m from the two hypotheses and use their product as the witness.
